data.description: Existing browser used by uploaders and reviewers; outside provisioning scope. The application authenticates staff and enforces separate upload and reviewer permissions.

data.label: Invoice intake and approval
data.description: Composed invoice-workflow deployment unit on Azure Container Apps, owning browser/API, background worker and isolated PDF/OCR parser. Internal generated resources include Azure Database for PostgreSQL durable queue/outbox and review state, private versioned Azure Blob Storage originals, staff sign-in and separate workload identities, regional model integration, and operating tasks/monitoring. Extract supplier, invoice date, total and currency with source evidence; incomplete or failed extraction stays visible for review. Commit workflow state and queued work transactionally; use bounded retries and recover stalled work. Bind reviewer approval to the exact result revision and delivery payload. Send with a stable operation identity; uncertain accounting outcomes are fenced for reconciliation rather than blindly resent. Accounting must independently pass the normalized-action-v1 and durable idempotency contract. Parser isolation, destination model policy, retention, backup/restore, operating ownership and native regional availability require qualification; this diagram proves no deployment.

REQ-001 — must functional other: Accept uploaded PDF invoices, asynchronously extract supplier, invoice date, total and currency, and persist results in a review queue. Proposed acceptance: show supporting evidence and expose incomplete extraction or processing failures for correction. (open)

REQ-002 — must functional security: Permit accounting submission only after an authorized reviewer approves the exact result revision and delivery payload; changes invalidate that approval. Enforce reviewer permissions on the server and retain the approval and delivery history. (open)

REQ-003 — must nonfunctional reliability: Repeated delivery and worker recovery must not create duplicate accounting invoices. Persist stable operation and payload identities, require a qualified destination idempotency contract, and reconcile uncertain external outcomes before allowing another submission. (open)
